misconception.text: A pendulum swings faster when it is given a bigger push.

correction.text: The period of a pendulum does not depend on the push. It depends on the length and on gravity.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: A wave carries energy along with it.

correction.text: A wave carries energy but not matter. The medium stays where it is, and the energy travels through it.

misconception.text: Light always travels in straight lines.

correction.text: Light is a wave and it spreads. It travels straight only when the object is far enough away that the spreading does not matter.

misconception.text: Two beams of light crossing produce a bright spot where they cross.

correction.text: They pass through each other. The bright fringes of an interference pattern come from the two beams overlapping, not from them colliding.
